featuredProject.title: Nabodigonto
featuredProject.summary: Flagship community and financial management platform for Nabodigonto Social Welfare Organization. Features blind audit double-signed treasury verification, dynamic 3D flip digital member ID cards with QR verification, dues tracking, and transparent financial reporting.
highlights: Real production platform engineered for a registered social welfare organization, resulting in executive appointment as IT Secretary
Blind Audit Protocol: double-signed verification keeping treasury totals masked until dual officer sign-off
Dynamic 3D flip member ID cards with public QR verification and bulk PVC print layouts
Dues tracking ledger with automated receipt generation and SHA-256 verified PDF audit reports
Serverless deployment on Cloudflare Workers edge via OpenNext with Neon PostgreSQL and Clerk v7
featuredProject.problem: Nabodigonto Social Welfare Organization previously handled member dues and community welfare contributions using manual paper records and spreadsheets. This led to reconciliation delays, lack of public verification, and the risk of discrepancy in treasury reports.
featuredProject.technicalApproach: Architected a full-stack serverless web platform on Next.js 16 deployed to Cloudflare Workers via OpenNext. Used Neon Serverless PostgreSQL with Prisma ORM for relational integrity, and integrated Clerk v7 for multi-role access control spanning members, financial auditors, and executive officers.
challenges: Enforcing an uncompromising audit policy so that no single officer could unilaterally reveal or modify financial balance totals.
Generating high-resolution (300 DPI) printable PVC membership ID cards with embedded QR verification completely client-side to minimize server resource costs.
Adapting Next.js App Router server actions and Prisma connection pooling within edge worker lifecycle constraints.
keyDecisions: Double-Signed Verification State Machine: Treasury balances remain strictly masked until both the Finance Officer and Executive Admin supply their authenticated approvals.
Neon Serverless Postgres: Chose over local SQLite edge storage for robust transactional consistency, multi-table audit joins, and reliable connection pooling.
Client-Side PDF Compilation: Leveraged browser canvas and PDF generation libraries to export receipts and ID cards without incurring edge compute costs.
featuredProject.result: Successfully launched into production as the organization's official operational backbone. Appointed IT Secretary by the executive board to oversee system governance, feature rollouts, and technical stewardship.

highlights: End-to-end learning lifecycle supporting course catalogs, student enrollments, lessons, and interactive exams
Bilingual parity (EN/BN) across administrative dashboards and student learning interfaces
Cloudflare R2 integration for lecture resources and Neon Serverless Postgres with Drizzle ORM
Edge-rendered and deployed globally via Cloudflare Workers
featuredProject.problem: Educators in Bangladesh often rely on scattered platforms (Facebook groups, Google Drives, third-party form builders) to deliver course materials and conduct exams, creating a fragmented experience with high dropout rates and no unified progress tracking.
featuredProject.technicalApproach: Built a unified EdTech platform with Next.js 16 edge rendering, Drizzle ORM for lightweight and type-safe database queries against Neon Postgres, and Cloudflare R2 object storage for lecture assets.

featuredProject.title: ARVAANA
featuredProject.summary: A modern luxury fragrance e-commerce platform crafted for artisanal alcohol-free attars and inspired perfumes in Bangladesh. Features zero-FOUC dual themes, multi-tier bottle volume pricing, and a zero-friction WhatsApp concierge checkout flow.
highlights: Zero-friction WhatsApp Concierge Checkout converting high-intent local shoppers across all 64 districts in Bangladesh with automated BDT price and variant encoding
Dynamic multi-size variant engine (6ML, 15ML, 30ML, 50ML) with real-time client-side price computation and discount badges
Custom luxury dark emerald (#051811) and minimalist pearl white theme system with zero flash of unstyled content (FOUC)
Full JSON-LD Schema.org @graph implementation establishing verified brand entity and creator attribution
featuredProject.problem: Traditional e-commerce carts suffer from high abandonment in Bangladesh due to mandatory account creation, credit card requirements, and multi-step OTP forms, whereas local fragrance consumers prefer conversational ordering with immediate customer service.
featuredProject.technicalApproach: Created a high-performance Next.js 16 web storefront tailored for emerging market consumer behavior. The checkout encodes selected variants, delivery district, delivery fees, and order totals directly into a structured WhatsApp message payload.
challenges: Eliminating theme flicker (FOUC) between the deep emerald dark theme and pearl light theme on initial page load.
Calculating dynamic pricing tiers and volume discounts instantaneously without layout shift (zero CLS).
keyDecisions: Conversational WhatsApp Checkout: Replaced traditional payment gateways with automated URL-encoded WhatsApp messages, matching local purchasing habits.
Static Generation with Client Hydration: Rendered product catalogs statically for fast page loads, keeping variant calculations responsive in client state.
featuredProject.result: Launched a production luxury fragrance store serving customers nationwide with intuitive multi-variant pricing and seamless mobile ordering.

featuredProject.title: Quiz Management & Examination System
featuredProject.summary: Desktop examination application developed in Java and JavaFX for the Design Patterns Lab Final Project (Mini-SPL) at IIT, University of Dhaka. Implements rigorous GoF patterns, role-based workflows, and SQLite relational persistence.
highlights: Implementation of GoF patterns: Strategy (scoring), State (quiz lifecycle), Factory (questions), Observer (timer/events)
Role-based dashboards for Teachers (quiz authoring, question bank, analytics) and Students (exam taking, result review)
Support for 4 question types: MCQ, True/False, Fill-in-the-Blank, and Multiple Answer
Full SQLite persistence via JDBC with automated schema migration and database seeder
featuredProject.problem: Academic testing systems often suffer from rigid scoring rules, hardcoded question types, and tightly coupled UI and business logic that make codebase maintenance and testing difficult.
featuredProject.technicalApproach: Engineered a modular desktop application in Java 17 and JavaFX 21 applying classic Gang of Four (GoF) object-oriented design patterns to cleanly separate concerns and ensure testability with JUnit 5.
challenges: Coordinating quiz timer events, countdown warnings, and auto-submission across asynchronous JavaFX application threads.
Designing polymorphic database schemas and JDBC queries to support multiple distinct question types.
keyDecisions: Strategy Pattern for Scoring: Allows switching between standard scoring, negative marking, and weighted points without altering exam runner code.
State Pattern for Exam Lifecycle: Modeled quiz states (Not Started, In Progress, Paused, Submitted, Graded) to prevent invalid state transitions.
Factory Pattern for Questions: Decoupled UI question component instantiation from question data models.
featuredProject.result: Completed and presented as the final Mini-SPL course project at IIT DU, achieving clean automated test coverage and seamless multi-role examination workflows.

featuredProject.title: Mosque Library Management
featuredProject.summary: A full-stack web application for managing mosque libraries — Islamic book catalog browsing, member issue/return tracking, and committee role assignments with bilingual (EN/BN) support.
highlights: Comprehensive Islamic book catalog with search, categorization, and availability tracking
Member borrowing lifecycle with due dates, loan renewals, and overdue alerts
Bilingual English and Bengali localization for seamless community accessibility
featuredProject.problem: Community mosque libraries frequently encounter lost books, untracked loans, and manual paper records, making it difficult for patrons to discover available literature.
featuredProject.technicalApproach: Developed a modern web portal using Next.js, TypeScript, and Prisma ORM backed by PostgreSQL, with responsive layouts in Tailwind CSS and bilingual language support.
challenges: Managing book loan states (Issued, Overdue, Returned, Lost) and renewal limits.
Providing quick search across both Bengali and English book titles and author names.
keyDecisions: Relational Schema: Enforced strict foreign keys connecting books, copies, members, and loan transactions to maintain audit integrity.
Bilingual UI Localization: Built lightweight dictionary-based localization to cater to both local and international patrons.
featuredProject.result: Delivered an accessible web catalog and lending management system ready for community library operations.

projects.title: Quran Reading Tracker
projects.summary: An offline-first Android mobile application built with React Native and Expo to cultivate and track daily Quran reading habits with complete privacy and local data persistence.
highlights: Dual independent tracking pipelines: Arabic recitation (Surah + Ruku) and Bangla translation (Surah + Ayat)
100% offline-first privacy with zero trackers, zero cloud dependencies, and local AsyncStorage persistence
Daily streak calculators, reading target meters, and smooth dark-mode UI with Islamic aesthetics
Automated build workflow via Expo EAS for Android APK distribution
projects.problem: Existing Quran tracking apps frequently require cloud logins, display intrusive advertisements, and bundle third-party analytics trackers that compromise user privacy.
projects.technicalApproach: Engineered an offline-first mobile app using React Native, TypeScript, and Expo. State and daily progress are serialized directly to local AsyncStorage with zero network requests.
challenges: Decoupling the distinct progress systems for Arabic recitation (measured in Rukus) and Bengali translation (measured in individual Ayats).
Calculating uninterrupted reading streaks and habit velocity accurately across arbitrary timezone adjustments.
keyDecisions: Zero-Network Architecture: No server backend, no authentication wall, and no telemetry SDKs — guaranteeing user privacy.
Optimistic Local State: UI updates immediately upon completion with asynchronous disk persistence.
projects.result: Shipped a clean, lightweight Android application with daily habit tracking, streak preservation, and complete offline autonomy.

projects.title: image-comparison
projects.summary: Contributed to romankh3/image-comparison, an open-source Java visual QA testing library on Maven Central, as a University Software Engineering assignment (PR #255). Refactored recursive region traversal to iterative ArrayDeque and optimized coordinate checks.
highlights: Replaced recursive difference grouping with iterative ArrayDeque BFS, eliminating StackOverflowError on high-resolution diffs
Optimized memory allocation by replacing per-pixel Point objects with primitive coordinate evaluation
Maintained 100% test suite pass rate (66/66 JUnit tests) with zero PMD/CPD quality violations
projects.problem: The library's difference-grouping algorithm used a recursive flood-fill algorithm that risked triggering StackOverflowError when analyzing high-resolution image differences, while allocating millions of transient Point objects that triggered frequent garbage collection pauses.
projects.technicalApproach: Refactored the core region identification algorithm into an iterative Breadth-First Search (BFS) using Java's ArrayDeque, avoiding call-stack exhaustion, and evaluated coordinates directly via primitive values.
challenges: Ensuring the refactored iterative algorithm generated pixel-for-pixel identical difference bounding boxes as the original recursive implementation.
Passing strict upstream static analysis gates (Checkstyle, PMD, and CPD) without introducing regressions.
keyDecisions: Iterative ArrayDeque BFS: Completely eliminated recursion depth limits, enabling comparison of large 4K+ images without stack limits.
Primitive Coordinate Packing: Replaced redundant Point object instantiations to reduce GC allocation pressure.
projects.result: Submitted upstream as Pull Request #255, passing all 66 unit tests, satisfying code quality checks, and fulfilling an advanced university Software Engineering open-source assignment.

projects.title: TetriC
projects.summary: A modular, console-based multiplayer Tetris game built in C for a university Software Engineering project. Features single-player, local two-player, and socket-based network multiplayer over TCP.
highlights: Console-based Tetris implemented in pure C with matrix rotation and collision algorithms
Local two-player and socket-based network multiplayer over TCP
Dynamic score progression, levels, and persistent high score leaderboards
projects.problem: Implementing real-time interactive multiplayer in a resource-constrained terminal environment requires strict frame timing, low-latency socket networking, and cross-platform terminal I/O handling in pure C.
projects.technicalApproach: Built a modular ANSI terminal game engine in C with matrix-based collision detection, non-blocking keyboard input, and POSIX TCP socket networking for two-player duels.
challenges: Synchronizing piece drop ticks and line clears between two separate network machines without gameplay jitter.
Handling ANSI terminal escape codes cleanly across Linux and Windows command-line environments without screen tearing.
keyDecisions: Non-blocking I/O with select(): Enabled concurrent handling of player keypresses and incoming network socket packets.
Compact Binary Network Protocol: Encoded board states and line-clear events into lightweight fixed-size binary structs.
projects.result: Successfully created and demonstrated a responsive, network-capable terminal Tetris game for a university Software Engineering project.
